name: canvas.read
summary: Everything on the canvas, cards included, each with its box; an item cut by a frame round it that clips says `clipped: "partly"` (some of its box is outside) or `"fully"` (none is inside), as does a text whose words overflow its fixed width and height. A card is { type: "card", card: <path>, box } (an old board, { type: "board", board }); every other item has pen.dev's own fields. Read it before placing anything. `frame: "frames/<name>"` reads a frame file instead, its items in its own space; this and the item calls below take `frame` in place of `canvas`, and a change to a frame shows on every canvas placing it. `of` (an id, a board's path, or an id inside an instance such as "card-1/label") reads that one item and what is in it; `depth` keeps that many levels of children (0: the items alone), and an item whose children were left out says how many in `childCount`. `resolve` works values out instead of reading them as written, each off by default: `variables` puts each $name's value in, for the light theme or `theme` ({ mode: "dark" }); `instances` reads a ref as its expanded copy, overrides applied, its items under `children` with ids "ref/child"; `geometry` adds a path's or shape's `outline`, an SVG path in its own space (0,0 its top-left corner).
signature: canvas.read(options?: { canvas?: string; frame?: string; of?: string; depth?: number; resolve?: { variables?: boolean; instances?: boolean; geometry?: boolean }; theme?: Record<string, string> })
returns: { canvas?: string; frame?: string; title?: string; file?: string; version: string; rev?: number; error?: string; variables?: Record<string, unknown>; themes?: Record<string, unknown>; items: Item[] }

name: canvas.space
summary: Where a box of `size` fits: the top-left corner nearest the middle of everything on the canvas where the box, grown by `margin` (160) on every side, touches no top-level item (arrows aside). With `near` (an id or a card's path) it starts on that item's `side` (right; or below, left, above), tops or lefts aligned as beside and below do, and steps outward past whatever is in the way. Nothing is placed: give the corner to insert or move as `at`.
signature: canvas.space(size: { w: number; h: number }, options?: { canvas?: string; frame?: string; near?: string; side?: "right" | "below" | "left" | "above"; margin?: number })

name: canvas.insert
summary: Add an item to the canvas. A card is { type: "card", card: <its folder or index.html> }, or { type: "card", html, title?, width?, height? } to write one and place it; anything else is a pen.dev item (note, text, frame, rectangle, ellipse, arrow, ref). Say where: `at` is its top-left corner; `beside` or `below` (an item's id or a card's path) puts it 160 px clear of that item, tops or lefts aligned; `parent` and `index` put it inside a frame. An item with a `name` and no `id` takes its name as its id ("Pricing card" → pricing-card, then pricing-card-2), its children too; the answer has every id.

name: canvas.batch
summary: Several of the changes above in one call, applied together or not at all. Each op is the call of that name with its item or id inside: { op: "insert", item, beside }, { op: "update", id, set }, { op: "delete", id }. A later op can be beside an item an earlier one made. pen.dev's own form, { op: "insert", node, box }, is taken too. This and insert, update and replace add a note for each field an item's type does not have, and each value Decks keeps for pen.dev but does not draw (shader and mesh_gradient fills, background_blur and shader effects, inner shadows on anything but a box or a whole ellipse, script items); nothing is refused for it.

name: canvas.screenshot
summary: A picture of the canvas, or part of it: drawing and cards together, saved to `file`. `of` is an item's id, a card's path, a list of them, or a box; one card's path alone is that card as the person's browser has it now, without the drawing round it. A .pen file's path pictures that file whole. The picture is the area at one pixel per canvas unit, shrunk until its long side is at most 1,600 px; `scale` multiplies that, so `scale: 2` of a 1,000 px card is 2,000 px wide and of a 7,500 px row is 3,200. `format` "jpeg" or "pdf", and `to` a path in the deck (`exports/plan.png`), make a file to hand on. Drawn natively over each card's current picture (`how` "native"), or in the browser with live cards when asked (`live: true`) or when it must be: math, a picture it cannot load, a card not yet pictured, a PDF (`how` "chromium: <why>").
signature: canvas.screenshot(options?: { canvas?: string; of?: string | string[] | { x1?: number; y1?: number; x2?: number; y2?: number }; scale?: number; format?: "png" | "jpeg" | "pdf"; to?: string; scheme?: "light" | "dark"; live?: boolean })

name: canvas.export
summary: The items `of` names (an id or a list, each with what is in it) as one self-contained web page in the deck, at `to` (default `exports/<id>.html`). A frame with a layout is a flexbox (gap, padding, justifyContent, alignItems; fill_container is flex 1 or stretch, fit_content the content's size), a number is px, and a frame with no layout holds its children where they sit; text keeps its font, size, weight, line height, letter spacing, colour and wrapping; fills (colours, gradients, pictures by relative address), strokes, corners, outer shadows and opacity are CSS; icons, paths and shapes are inline SVG; variables are CSS custom properties, with the dark theme's values under prefers-color-scheme. `format` "html" (the default) writes inline styles; "tailwind" the same page as Tailwind classes, with Tailwind's CDN script.
